definitions.meaning: first meaning: to halt or restrain a flow
second meaning: the stalk holding up a flower or leaf

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like an instruction to inspect a brace; each is a separate meaning of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means stop a flow, as with bleeding; as a noun it is the stalk bearing a plant's leaves.

clue.text: Prolonged trouble when the man grabs lass naughtily

indicators.note: to grab something is to hold it inside one's grip, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the man is referred to as he

indicators.note: behaving naughtily means not keeping in line, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man getting fresh with a girl causes lasting bother.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassle is a drawn-out annoyance or bother, ongoing difficulty that wears a person down.

clue.text: The old-fashioned you, in humour lacking

indicators.note: 'in' places the first item inside the following word

explanation.surface: Someone tells an old-fashioned person they have no sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: Thou is the archaic form of you, still heard in old prayers and poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a preposition, it means not having something, as in going short of food or money.

clue.text: More attractive invitation — that is received by both sides

indicators.note: something received by others is taken in between them, so a piece sits inside

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: An offer to join someone is welcomed from all quarters, making it more appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Comely is an old word for good-looking or pleasing to the eye; this is its comparative form.

clue.text: Lift a table in the restaurant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small elevator carrying food between floors
second meaning: a stand or side table used for serving dishes

explanation.surface: A diner is told to pick up a table in the eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like a verb acting on the table; it is a noun, the British word for an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a small hatch elevator for food and a revolving serving stand placed near diners.

clue.text: Grass shoots up? That's grass for you

indicators.note: in a down clue going up reverses the word, and the question says the result is still the same plant

parts.note: a coastal grass that binds sand dunes

explanation.surface: A remark on how grass sprouts upwards, with a shrug that grass is like that.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upwards in the grid this plant's name spells the same thing, so the grass going up is still grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is the tough grass planted on sand dunes to stabilise them against wind erosion.

clue.text: Beef and butter dunked in gently sparkling wine

parts.note: p for piano, the musical direction to play softly

indicators.note: something dunked in a drink ends up inside it

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
a ram is an animal that butts

explanation.surface: A recipe of beef and butter soaked in mild fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but a creature that butts: the ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked brisket, a cured cut usually made from cattle meat.

clue.text: A viewer's jolly when the leader's taken off

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, and taking it off removes it

explanation.surface: Someone watching is cheerful once the boss has left.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is the eyepiece of a microscope or telescope, the lens one looks through.

clue.text: Ruin brings the reverse of humour

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a humour is a state of mind or temper

explanation.surface: Destruction leads to the opposite of good cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a terrible fate or downfall from which there is no recovery.

clue.text: One composer chosen for new orchestration ahead of another

indicators.note: one piece comes before the other, placed in front
a new orchestration rearranges music, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer is selected to rescore a piece before a second one is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for another composer, picking up the definition word: Berg was Schoenberg's pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Schoenberg was the Austrian creator of twelve-tone music, a major figure of the twentieth century.

clue.text: See 13
In icy cavern Eddie explodes bomb

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: every letter of these words is the raw material

explanation.surface: In a frozen cave, a man named Eddie sets off an explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a weapon designed to start fires, a firebomb rather than one relying on blast.

clue.text: Indignant, but better prepared for war?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: having taken up weapons

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is a literal reading of an idiom: arms are weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes people loudly protesting, while literally it pictures soldiers holding weapons ready to fight.

clue.text: University official favouring Conservative to the Right

indicators.note: 'to the' attaches the last piece onto the end of the others

explanation.surface: A college officer leans towards the Tories on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge, this officer is responsible for student discipline and order.

clue.text: The first words from 24 down for the shrub?

wordplay.note: 24 down is Hero, the lover in Greek myth, who might begin by calling her beloved

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks what Hero might say on seeing a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth, Leander swam the Hellespont each night to reach his lover Hero, a priestess; her opening cry to him spells the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a poisonous evergreen Mediterranean bush with pink or white flowers.

clue.text: Performer (Eastern) about to ensnare one with obscene stuff

indicators.note: 'about' means turned around, so the combination is read backwards
to ensnare something is to trap it inside, so a piece goes within

explanation.surface: An Eastern performer is about to trap someone with filth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers sexually explicit books, pictures or art intended to arouse.

clue.text: Agreement a letter changed for one of the lessees

indicators.note: a single letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a covenant is a formal agreement

explanation.surface: A tenancy agreement is altered by one letter for a lessee.
explanation.walkthrough: The V of the agreement is replaced by a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharing a lease with another tenant is one of the joint renters of a property.

clue.text: Street jewellery — pearls and more pearls?

explanation.surface: Jewellery bought on the high street: pearls upon pearls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengths of threaded beads worn as necklaces; the question mark admits it is a definition by example.

clue.text: Mournful-sounding bloke is behind the scheme

indicators.note: one piece placed behind the other comes after it

explanation.surface: A sad-voiced man is the one behind the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a loud, resonant tone that is melancholy, like a tolling bell.

clue.text: The French fabric for covering cold window

indicators.note: a covering goes around what it covers, so a piece sits inside

explanation.surface: French fabric is used to drape a chilly window.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancet is a tall, narrow pointed-arch window typical of Gothic church architecture.

clue.text: Supernatural being disturbed priest

indicators.note: something disturbed is knocked out of its proper order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A ghostly figure has rattled a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf, fairy or similar spirit from folklore.

clue.text: Lustre on a lady

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it

explanation.surface: A woman's hair or dress has a shine to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheena is a woman's first name; a crossword lady is often any female name.

clue.text: Succession of individuals providing documentation on a country?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people walking one behind another
second meaning, taken literally: a dossier about an Asian nation

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the whimsical second reading: a file on India.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means people moving in single line, one after another, as on a narrow path.

clue.text: One wanting to protect a vixen could be nuts about her

definitions.text: One wanting to protect a vixen

indicators.note: 'could be' says the following words might become something else once their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A fox-lover is said to be crazy about the vixen she adores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts about her' reads as an idiom for being smitten, but it is the raw material. A vixen is a female fox, quarry of the British fox hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Such activists disrupt fox hunts so that the hounds cannot catch and kill the animal.

clue.text: Celebrated man is all but a tyrant

indicators.note: all but means nearly the whole, so the last letter is lost

explanation.surface: A famous figure turns out to be almost a despot.
explanation.definitionFit: A man admired and celebrated for courage or great achievements is a champion figure.

clue.text: Command issued in successive notes to tribe

parts.note: D and E follow each other in the musical scale
the Cree are a North American people

explanation.surface: An order given in a string of notes to a tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: An official order with legal force, issued by a ruler or court.

clue.text: Corruption with criminal bunch ne'er reforming

parts.note: a gang is a group of criminals

indicators.note: reforming something remakes it in a new shape, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Corruption alongside a crooked crew who will never go straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangrene is the decay and death of body tissue, a literal rotting of the flesh.
